home.title: The place you practice ECGs.
home.lead: A real ECG every week, three new papers explained in two minutes and, soon, an app with hundreds of ECGs marked by a cardiologist trained in electrophysiology. In English and Romanian.
home.signup_heading: Get the ECG of the week
home.weekly_intro: Every email looks like this: a real trace, four options and the answer explained step by step.

home.get_heading: What you get, free, once a week

get_items.title: One ECG to read
get_items.text: A real trace, one question, four options. The answer comes at the end of the email, explained step by step.

get_items.title: Three papers in two minutes
get_items.text: The week's important new papers, summarised in our own words, with a link to each article.

get_items.title: One practical tip
get_items.text: What to watch on the monitor, where the electrodes go, when to call the doctor. Short and concrete.

home.gift_title: Sign-up gift: the ECG pocket guide
home.gift_text: 11 printable cards: the systematic read, normal values, axis, blocks, STEMI criteria, tachycardias, electrolytes and pacemakers.
home.app_intro: ECG courses show you traces. The app makes you read them: a few minutes a day, with instant feedback.
home.calipers_text: Drag the two lines onto the peaks of two R waves. We measure the interval and the rate, just like on paper.

features.title: Hundreds of real, marked ECGs
features.text: From open databases and anonymised teaching cases. Every answer is checked by a cardiologist.

features.title: Spaced repetition
features.text: See each ECG again just as you're about to forget it. Ten minutes a day is enough.

features.title: Digital calipers and measurement drills
features.text: PR, QRS, QT and QTc, axis. Measure on the trace and see how close you were.

features.title: Pacemakers and devices
features.text: Pacing, capture, sensing, pacing modes. What's missing almost everywhere, explained by an electrophysiologist.

features.title: An AI tutor, labelled as AI
features.text: It explains the teaching ECGs from explanations the doctor has approved. It never reads your own or your patients' ECGs.

features.title: Rhythm strips and monitor mode
features.text: For ICU, emergency and ambulance staff: rhythms that scroll like the bedside monitor.

home.about_text: Every ECG, every answer and every paper summary passes the doctor's desk before it reaches you.
rules: Education only: we never read personal ECGs or give individual medical advice.
Paper summaries are drafted with AI and checked by the doctor, with a link to the source.
ECGs come from licensed open databases (PTB-XL, CC BY 4.0) or from anonymised cases published with permission.

faq.a: Nothing. The weekly email and the ECG pocket guide are free.
Not yet. We're working on a credited programme with an accredited partner and will tell you by email when it exists.

faq.q: Can I send you my own or a patient's ECG?
faq.a: No. Everything here is education only and doesn't replace medical care. For a real ECG, see your own doctor.
Once a week. Unsubscribe with one click from any email.

faq.q: What data do you keep about me?
faq.a: Your email address, your first name if you give it, and your role, so you get the right version. The data stays on servers in the European Union.
